A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SSSD and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting comparison. All pages were inspected, including v2 Appendices A–C; v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original candidate-acceptance, retrieval-time, sampling, and latency/throughput experiments using Llama2-7b and Llama3-8B.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original ablations, cold-start and multilingual experiments, reasoning evaluations, and serving-performance results, including Llama-3.3-70B experiments.

M1.justification: v2 extends v1’s fixed external datastore with online accumulation of outputs from past conversations and oldest-entry eviction, enabling empty-store startup and adaptation during serving (Section 3.1.2). This changes the method’s operation beyond the per-request prompt/self-output trie already present in v1. The underlying CPU retrieval and candidate-tree fusion approach remains.

E1.justification: v2 retains MT-Bench, GSM8k, and PG-19, but removes the Natural Questions short-query and Dolly-15k evaluations. It adds HumanEval code generation, SWE-Bench agentic workloads, MATH-500 including extended reasoning, and multilingual MT-Bench translations. Cold-start and language-adaptation scenarios substantially broaden the evaluated conditions.

E2.justification: v1 compares candidate quality against REST and PIA, and end-to-end performance against autoregressive decoding and PIA. v2 adds evaluated PLD, EAGLE-2, EAGLE-3, and Llama-3.2-1B draft-model baselines; REST also enters end-to-end comparisons. PIA and v2’s Lookahead refer to the same Zhao et al. method and are matched as a retained comparator.

E3.justification: The customized vLLM/Ascend setup is replaced by SGLang/GPU experiments using newer 8B models, Qwen3-14B, and Llama-3.3-70B. New protocols include prefill/decode disaggregation, tensor parallelism, and stochastic reasoning generation up to 4096 tokens. Single-device totals still include prefill, whereas distributed plots report inter-token latency. These changes prevent treating the results as same-setting reruns.

E4.justification: The candidate-source ablation is retained and revised, while v2 adds datastore-size sensitivity, empty versus English-initialized datastores, language adaptation, and model-generated versus dataset-answer comparisons (Figure 4). Lookahead receives warm/cold-cache analysis. v1’s tokenizer comparison, temperature sweep, and empirical operator-cost breakdown are removed rather than relocated.

E5.justification: v2 first specifies averages over five runs for the Qwen3-14B experiments in Figure 4 and the reasoning experiment in Figure 5f. v1 supplies no corresponding repeated-run counts. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests. This is additional run reporting, not evidence that previously reported experiments received more runs.

E6.justification: Much of the empirical evidence is replaced or expanded. For example, v1 Figure 6 reports 2.05x PG-19 speedup for Llama2-7b at batch size 1 and approximately 3400-token inputs. v2 Table 1 reports SSSD speedups of 1.23x/1.26x versus EAGLE-3’s 0.80x/1.09x for Llama-3.1-8B/Llama-3.3-70B with disaggregation and inputs up to 40k tokens. v2 also adds a 2.29x reasoning speedup. Different conditions preclude direct performance-change conclusions.

T1.justification: v1 Table 1 assumes equal query and KV head counts. v2 Appendix B and Table 2 introduce explicit GQA group size and tensor-parallel size into the FLOP/IO derivations, revise MLP accounting, and change approximate attention intensity from 2sq to 2gsq. The resulting attention-versus-linear-layer bounds extend the mathematical model substantially beyond relocating the existing roofline discussion.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes scalable lookup decoding, fourfold throughput at fixed short-context latency, and effectiveness across tasks. v2 makes deployment without data preparation, cold-start operation, automatic language/domain adaptation, and robustness under distribution shift central contributions. Its abstract and conclusion also foreground competitiveness with trained approaches. This substantially changes the contribution emphasis and scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking adaptation to model-generated datastore contents and long-context advantages to approximately constant drafting cost without a draft KV-cache. It explains cases where EAGLE-3 performs better. The new Limitations section qualifies v1’s optimistic MoE discussion and adds MLA-kernel, CPU, and host-memory constraints; Appendix B explicitly excludes communication costs. Privacy and cross-language performance implications are also newly discussed.

D1.justification: Appendix A expands the single merging pseudocode into retrieval and merging algorithms with explicit thresholds and dampening constants. v2 adds datastore, generation, and deployment details, including a 13 GB datastore, and promises code release upon acceptance without establishing public availability. Some v1 details, including OpenMP and CPU identification, disappear. Appendix C’s TP = 2 description conflicts with Figure 6’s one-GPU-per-stage caption.

R1.justification: v2 substantially develops positioning around multilingual disparities, domain adaptation, EAGLE-3, and multi-token prediction, including a new Multilinguality subsection and references to Yi et al., Sandler et al., and Hong et al. The earlier hybrid-method discussion, including TriForce and Ouroboros, is removed. Publication updates to retained works such as REST and MagicDec are not treated as new research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around deployment and adaptation. Objectives become an explicit contributions list, evaluation sections are reorganized, and algorithm/hardware material moves into expanded appendices. Dedicated Limitations and Ethical considerations sections further change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1 with datastore-update machinery, combines revised hardware/speedup plots into Figure 2, and introduces cold-start and multilingual panels. Earlier latency–cost plots and throughput bars give way to multi-baseline latency–throughput grids. The hardware table moves to Appendix B with revised rows, and a PG-19 results table is added. Typography, headers, and abstract layout also change.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for deployment and competitiveness claims that v1 tested mainly with small models and lookup baselines. Direct trained-drafter comparisons, 70B serving experiments, and cold-start, multilingual, and reasoning evaluations address that important evidence gap. Acknowledging EAGLE-3’s advantages and architectural/resource limitations also improves balance. These gains outweigh the removed temperature/tokenizer diagnostics, although conditional code release and inconsistent 70B configuration reporting leave reproducibility gaps.
